# Tiger Census
idk if eda is that useful for geospatial data 

```{r}
library(readr)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
tigercensus <- read_csv('~/data/2026-ASA-DataFest-Data-Files/tigercensuscodes.csv',show_col_types = FALSE)
determinants <- read_csv('~/data/2026-ASA-DataFest-Data-Files/social_determinants.csv',show_col_types = FALSE)
providers <- read_csv('~/data/2026-ASA-DataFest-Data-Files/providers.csv',show_col_types = FALSE)
patients <- read_csv('~/data/2026-ASA-DataFest-Data-Files/patients.csv',show_col_types = FALSE)
encounters <- read_csv('~/data/2026-ASA-DataFest-Data-Files/encounters.csv',show_col_types = FALSE)
diagnosis <- read_csv('~/data/2026-ASA-DataFest-Data-Files/diagnosis.csv',show_col_types = FALSE)
departments<- read_csv('~/data/2026-ASA-DataFest-Data-Files/departments.csv',show_col_types = FALSE)

tigercensus |> 
  dplyr::summarize(max = max(PopulationValue, na.rm = TRUE),
            min = min(PopulationValue, na.rm = TRUE),
            median = median(PopulationValue, na.rm = TRUE))

ggplot(tigercensus, aes(x = PopulationValue)) +
  geom_boxplot()
```
